grund: al-Muqsit is the one who acts with equity (qist) and gives the wronged their right; "Requiter" (one who repays) is a different meaning. Compare al-muqsitin, "those who act justly", in 49:9 and 60:8. Not the same as "The Just" (no. 30, al-Adl).
quellen: al-Ghazali, al-Maqsad al-asna, transl. D. Burrell and N. Daher (Islamic Texts Society, 1992), no. 86: "al-Muqsit, the Equitable"
T. P. Hughes, A Dictionary of Islam (1885), entry al-Muqsit: "The Equitable"

grund: al-Muqtadir names power over everything (intensive of al-Qadir), not determining. Burrell and Daher render it "the All-Determiner", but al-Ghazali himself counts it among the names that refer to power with something added. "The All-Powerful" (no. 69) and "The Omnipotent" (no. 10) are already taken.
quellen: T. P. Hughes, A Dictionary of Islam (1885), entry al-Muqtadir: "The Powerful or Prevailing"
Saheeh International (meal-en-saheeh) renders muqtadir in 54:42 and 54:55 as "Perfect in Ability"
al-Ghazali, al-Maqsad al-asna, transl. D. Burrell and N. Daher, part 2, ch. 1: al-Muqtadir among the names that refer to power

grund: Same mistake as in English: al-Muqtadir names power, not determining. "der Mächtige" (no. 69) and "der Allgewaltige" (no. 10) are already taken.
quellen: F. Bubenheim and N. Elyas, Der edle Qur'an (meal-de-bubenheim): muqtadir in 54:42 "Allmächtigen", in 54:55 "allmächtigen Herrscher"
